passages.text: Salvia japonica, known as East Asian sage, is an annual plant that is native to several provinces in China and Taiwan, growing at {{convert|200|to|1200|m|ft|abbr=on}} elevation. S. japonica grows on erect stems to {{convert|40|to|60|cm|in|abbr=on}} tall. Inflorescences are 2-6 flowered verticillasters in terminal racemes or panicles, with a corolla that varies in color from reddish, purplish, bluish, to white, and is approximately {{convert|1.2|cm|in|abbr=on}}.
There are two named varieties, with slight variations in leaf and flower shape: S. japonica var. japonica and S. japonica var. multifoliolata.
